The crew perceived abnormally low thrust but neither identified nor corrected the problem, with fatigue from jetlag suspected as contributing.
probable_cause: The thrust levers were never advanced to takeoff position, and the autothrust never transitioned to takeoff mode. The crew perceived through physical cues that thrust was abnormally low, but neither identified the problem nor took any corrective action. Simulations indicated that with timely corrective action, recovery and prevention of the accident was possible. Fatigue was suspected to be a contributing factor for all crew members.

title: American Airlines 331
summary: An American Airlines Boeing 737-823 overran runway 12 on landing at Kingston in poor weather. The aircraft touched down 4100 feet from threshold then continued through the perimeter fence at freeway speeds and broke apart on the beach. Contributing factors included the speed of the aircraft upon landing, tailwind conditions, a long touchdown well beyond the standard zone, and inadequate training on tailwind landings.
probable_cause: The crew's decision to land on runway 12 with a tailwind component, inadequate training on tailwind operations, and the aircraft's long touchdown point well beyond the standard zone resulted in runway overrun.

title: Northwest Airlines 253
summary: Northwest Airlines Flight 253, an Airbus A330 from Amsterdam Schiphol to Detroit Metropolitan Airport, was subjected to an attempted bombing on December 25, 2009. A 23-year-old Nigerian national Umar Farouk Abdulmutallab attempted to detonate an explosive device containing more than 80 grams of chemical explosives sewn into his underwear as the aircraft prepared to land. Passengers and crew subdued the attacker, with passenger Jasper Schuringa subduing Abdulmutallab after the explosive device activated but failed to detonate properly, sustaining first and second degree burns. The aircraft landed safely at Detroit Metropolitan Airport with no fatalities.
probable_cause: Deliberate terrorist attack using concealed chemical explosives that failed to detonate.
